title: Strong Complementarity
body_html:
Strong Complementarity

There exists an optimal pair $(x^*,y^*) \in X(A)\times Y(A)$ such that a pure row has positive probability under $x^*$ if and only if it is a best response to $y^*$, and a pure column has positive probability under $y^*$ if and only if it is a best response to $x^*$.
proof_html:
Write the row player's optimality problem as the linear program that maximizes $v$ subject to $$ xAe_j\ge v\quad (j\in J),\qquad x\in\Delta(I), $$ and write the dual column problem as the program that minimizes $w$ subject to $$ e_iAy\le w\quad (i\in I),\qquad y\in\Delta(J). $$ By linear-programming strong complementarity, there are optimal primal-dual solutions for which each primal slack is positive exactly when the corresponding dual variable is zero, and each dual slack is positive exactly when the corresponding primal variable is zero. Translating the slacks back to the matrix game, a row $i$ has zero probability in $x^*$ exactly when its payoff against $y^*$ is strictly below the value; hence $x_i^*>0$ exactly when row $i$ is a best response to $y^*$. Similarly, a column $j$ has zero probability in $y^*$ exactly when $x^*Ae_j$ is strictly above the value; hence $y_j^*>0$ exactly when column $j$ is a best response to $x^*$.

References

  • [MFoGT, Prop. 2.4.1(c)] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Existence of a strongly complementary optimal pair.
